newsitem.title: FINLAND: Banking stocks bolster thin Helsinki, UPM slips.
newsitem.headline: Banking stocks bolster thin Helsinki, UPM slips.

text.p: A healthy recovery in OKOBANK's January-September profits boosted hopes for the sector, helping the bourse to a slightly higher close on Monday but trade was thin ahead of U.S. elections on Tuesday, brokers said.
The HEX index rose 0.31 percent to 2,204.57 with volume just 159 million markka, 22 percent of it in Nokia, which closed 1.50 markka up at 210.50.
President Clinton was expected to be re-elected easily, but stock markets could be hit if Republicans lost control of both houses in Congress, brokers said.
Merita A ended fair trade 0.40 markka up at 13.70 as a clear improvement in domestic rival OKOBank sparked hopes for a strong report from Merita on Thursday.
OKO swung to a 248 million markka operating profit after credit losses from a 32 million year-ago loss.
Analysts' median forecast for Merita's January-September earnings due for release on November 7 was a 952 million markka operating profit after credit losses.
But UPM-Kymmene closed at a five-month low 89.40 markka, down 1.10 -- its lowest close since May 30 -- as more analysts downgraded international forestry stocks.
Ferry operator Silja closed flat at 32.00 markka after improved nine-month earnings, but trade was thin.
